title: Factorial Interaction Detective
scopeNote: This keeps the four editable cell means and the interaction plot, and adds the two things that decide whether the picture means anything: the axis scale and the uncertainty in each mean. The pattern presets, the additive-fit control, the read-it-the-other-way disclosure, the three-part prediction and the fill-in-the-sentence challenge stay in the longer version, and the page says so.
summary: A 2 by 2 design with four cell means the learner edits directly. Both main effects and the interaction update as arithmetic on those four numbers, and two further controls show how much of an apparent interaction is the axis it was drawn on and how much survives the uncertainty in the means.
learningObjectives: Define an interaction as a difference of differences and compute one from four cell means.
Explain why the interaction is the same number whichever factor is read as the moderator.
Recognise that the visual size of an interaction depends on the axis range chosen for the plot.
Judge an interaction against the uncertainty in the cell means rather than against its appearance.
Explain why main effects can be misleading in the presence of a crossover interaction.
interactionTypes: a live interaction plot with two lines
an axis-range control that changes the picture without changing the data
an uncertainty control that draws error bars and rescales the interaction into units of its own standard error
a withheld explanation released once the learner has changed the design
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Every figure is computed in the browser from the four numbers on screen and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with each cell mean a labelled number input and each presentation choice a native select. The plot carries a description giving all four cell means, both main effects, the interaction and, when a standard error is set, the interaction in units of its own standard error, so no conclusion depends on reading the lines. The two lines differ by dash pattern and end marker as well as by colour, and each is labelled at its right-hand end. The figure scrolls sideways rather than shrinking below legible label sizes on a narrow screen, and becomes a keyboard-reachable region when it does. Changes are announced through a polite live region. No timed content and no motion.
dataStatus: Fictional and illustrative. The four cell means describe an invented study of feedback timing and task complexity. They are not results, and the standard error is a value the learner chooses rather than one estimated from data.
simulationNotes: There is deliberately no F, no p and no effect size. Four cell means carry no information about within-cell variation or sample size, so a test statistic computed from them would be an invitation to over-read. Instead the interaction is reported in units of its own standard error: for four independent cell means each with standard error s, the difference of differences has standard error 2s. The starting values 70, 50, 50, 70 form an exact crossover, where both main effects are zero and the interaction carries everything.
readmeTopic: what an interaction is, and how much of the one you can see is the axis rather than the data
